items.title: Financial fraud discovered at an Essilor International group plant in Thailand; the financial impact was fully booked in the income statement for the 2019 fiscal year.
items.allegedBy: Internal finding by the group, disclosed in the 2019 annual results release
items.outcome: Financial impact of 185 M€ (net of FX effects) fully absorbed in the 2019 accounts; no public judicial or regulatory follow-up identified since.
items.source: Communiqué de résultats annuels 2019 d'EssilorLuxottica, 6 mars 2020

items.title: US antitrust class action (In re Eyewear Antitrust Litigation, S.D.N.Y.) alleging price-fixing orchestrated by EssilorLuxottica with dozens of co-defendant luxury brands, aimed at artificially inflating eyewear prices by up to 1000%.
items.allegedBy: Plaignants privés (class action), cabinets d'avocats plaignants américains
items.outcome: Motion to dismiss granted on 26 September 2025, the judge finding the 'premium eyewear' market definition advanced by the plaintiffs implausible; the latter had one last opportunity to file an amended complaint (deadline 17 October 2025).
items.source: Law360 (26 septembre 2025) ; Justia, In re Eyewear Antitrust Litigation, No. 1:24-cv-04826 (S.D.N.Y.)

compliance.note: No regulatory investigation (SEC/DOJ) and no ongoing allegation of accounting or financial fraud identified to date. The only established fraud incident on record (Thailand, 2019) is old, one-off, and already absorbed in the accounts. The US antitrust litigation (2023) concerns an alleged price-fixing agreement, not accounting fraud - included here out of caution given its nature as an alleged seriously anticompetitive commercial practice and its still-open judicial status (search of 2026-08-06).

clesRetenues: Q Cardani (Intesa Sanpaolo) - drivers of smart glasses profitability in H1: the CFO reports a year-on-year improvement across every metric (average price, penetration of prescription/Transitions/polarised lenses, industrial productivity), an effect visible in the gross margin.
Q Cardani - operating expense trajectory and inflationary pressures in H2: the CFO sees no cause for concern, with costs deemed well under control for the rest of the year.

Q Dormois (Jefferies) - divergence in price positioning with the new Meta Glasses and the risk of opening up to other tech partners: the CEO replies that the portfolio already spans luxury down to mid-range, that Meta targets a younger, price-sensitive audience, and that no other partnership is contemplated beyond Meta at this stage.

Q Dormois - sequential AI glasses sales (Q2 vs Q1): the CFO specifies that the traditional core business is growing at the high end of the 'mid-single-digit' range (bolt-on M&A included), the remainder of Q2 growth (+8,7%) coming from smart glasses.

Q Solvet (BNP Paribas) - partnerships/supply agreements contemplated with other smart glasses manufacturers: the CEO presents the Applied Materials partnership as strategic, targeting a proprietary projection lens technology, positioning EssilorLuxottica in time as a supplier to other brands.
Q Solvet - tariff refunds received in H1, amount: the CFO confirms a net positive effect of 60 basis points on the gross margin in H1, combining new charges and refunds.

Q Smalley (Morgan Stanley) - clarification on the scale of the customs refunds in H2, whether the refund has already been received in full or a balance is still to come: the CFO says a residual amount of refunds is possible in H2, without quantifying it.

Q Smalley - H2 outlook by segment (Professional Solutions vs Direct to Consumer) and the July trend: the CFO cites a good month of July, a ramp-up in Stellest productivity in the United States (key accounts activated) and a dense innovation pipeline (Varilux, AI glasses, 2nd-generation Nuance Audio, Meta launches) as reasons for optimism despite a demanding comparison base.

Q Al-Wakeel (Barclays) - margin impact of the low-price Meta Glasses launch and confirmation of lens exclusivity for Meta: the CEO confirms that EssilorLuxottica remains the exclusive lens manufacturer for Meta and that the margin impact is positive, with the shared technology platform reducing costs as volumes rise.

Q Al-Wakeel - order of magnitude of the gross customs refund (~300 M€) and the risk of memory/component cost inflation for 2027: the CFO neither confirms nor denies the figure put forward, says he sees no cost headwind at this stage and expects wearables margin progression to continue in H2.

Q Dubajova (Citi) - gap between the double-digit growth comment made in April and Q2 performance, areas of consumer slowdown: the CFO reports a non-material Q1/Q2 gap, some softening at certain North American B2B key accounts, but still a 6-month view at the high end of the 'high-single-digit' range for the region, explained by a sell-in/sell-out timing effect.

Q Dubajova - update on myopia adoption in the United States and the weight of the United States in global myopia revenue: the Deputy CEO reports global myopia growth of +25% in H1 26 (against +22% in 2025), with China accounting for 75% of the total (vs 80% in 2025), the United States being at an early adoption stage with 11 000 active points of sale and media support planned in H2.
Q Cota (BofA) - structural benefit expected from the decline in tariffs, more visible in 2027: the CFO says that H2 26 tariffs are slightly below last year's, without being materially lower.

Q Cota - risk of memory cost inflation on the wearables margin in 2027: the CFO attributes the cost dynamic to supply chain efficiency, the scale effect and the improving price mix, and expects margin progression to continue.

Q Ghilotti (Equita) - intellectual property of the Applied Materials partnership and time-to-market schedule: the CEO says the patents will be shared, that the partnership could evolve into a structural joint venture, and hopes to have products to sell as early as the beginning of next year (2027).

Q Ghilotti - gross margin trajectory in H2 excluding the effect of the customs refunds: the CFO confirms there are good reasons to see a positive gross margin trajectory in H2, beyond the customs effect alone.

engagementsStructurants.engagement: Strategic partnership with Applied Materials to develop smart optical systems (projection lenses) for AI/AR glasses; first products targeted for commercialisation as early as the beginning of 2027.
Launch of the first wearables production lines in Italy (Agordo site), with industrial operations targeted to start in early 2027.

epsReported.note: No per-share figure highlighted on the H1 call (semi-annual reporter); net profit margin +50bp cc with double-digit net profit growth at constant currency. Reported EPS to be anchored from the H1 2026 interim report at next refresh.

dernierCall.guidanceProchainTrimestre: No quantified quarterly guidance provided - the company communicates only qualitative annual and multi-year guidance.
dernierCall.guidanceAnnuelle: No formal quantified annual target; management is targeting solid organic growth at constant FX in H2 despite a demanding comparison base (H2 2025 had already accelerated to +15,2% at constant FX), with a gross and operating margin trajectory trending higher in the second half.
pointsCles: H1 revenue +9.7% at constant currency (Q2 +8.7%; core business 'upper mid-single-digit' incl. bolt-ons, smart eyewear nearly doubling and providing the balance) with adjusted operating profit +15% cc (18.6% margin) and record H1 free cash flow of EUR 1,067M - gross margin inflected to +10bp (vs -400bp+ dilution in H2 25), helped by price/mix and a NET POSITIVE 60bp tariff effect (Q1 charges vs H1 refunds; more refunds possible in H2, and the CFO commits qualitatively to a positive H2 gross-margin trajectory even excluding them).

Wearables economics keep improving on every KPI (average price, Rx/Transitions/polarized lens penetration, industrial productivity - category gross margin UP and visible in the numbers); EssilorLuxottica confirmed as EXCLUSIVE lens manufacturer for Meta, with the new lower-priced Meta-branded line (from $299) framed as deliberate segmentation toward younger consumers, not margin dilution; second-generation Nuance Audio lands mid-September.

Two long-term strategic options widened: the oculomics/medtech push (first integrated vision + eye-surgery center opened at LensCrafters Philadelphia, plan for surgical hubs on the store network, 50-minute OCT+RetinAI exams screening diabetes/cardiovascular/cognitive risk) and a strategic partnership with APPLIED MATERIALS on projection/electroactive lens systems for AI/AR wearables - shared IP, possible structural JV, pilot line in place, first product targeted for early 2027, with the stated ambition of becoming the strategic lens-component supplier to ALL smart-glasses makers.

Myopia management grew +25% worldwide in H1 (China ~75% of it): Stellest now in 11,000 US doors post-FDA with key-account activation and consumer media planned for H2 (US acceleration expected), Japan launched in June; watch items for H2: very demanding comp base (H2 25 +15.2% cc), soft Q2 at large North American B2B key accounts (read 6-month +HSD per CFO), flat France, negative luxury licenses - but July started well and FX could finally turn into a tailwind at current rates.

guidanceHistory.guidanceAnnuelle: No formal quantified annual target; solid organic growth targeted at constant FX in H2 despite a demanding comparison base, gross margin trending higher.

hypothese.guidanceLongTerme: New horizon (February 2026, replacing the 27-28 Md€ revenue / 19-20% adjusted margin target from the 2022 CMD, already exceeded on revenue but not on margin): over the next 5 years, at constant FX, solid revenue growth and adjusted operating margin progression broadly in line with that of revenue.
hypothese.summary: Vertically integrated global leader in optics and eyewear (Essilor+Luxottica+GrandVision), in the midst of a shift into med-tech (AI glasses with Meta, myopia, hearing, oculomics); strong structural growth, margin being rebuilt after the 2025 tariff trough.

ancrages.moteur: H1 26 grew 9,7% at constant FX, but H2 25 had already accelerated to +15,2% at constant FX (AI glasses effect) - this high base mechanically holds back reported growth in H2 26 despite intact operating momentum; the model assumes FY26 growth of around 8% at constant FX, brought down to ~5% at current FX given the weak dollar over H1.

The adjusted operating margin, having fallen to 16,0% at constant FX in 2025 (a trough tied to US tariffs and the AI glasses mix), is recovering in H1 26 (18,9% cc) thanks to the net positive effect of the customs refunds and to improving wearables productivity; the model assumes a GAAP operating margin close to 14,2-14,8% over 2026-2027 (a gap of around 350-400 bps versus the adjusted margin, tied to PPA amortisation).

Recurring amortisation of intangible assets arising from purchase price allocations (Essilor-Luxottica combination + GrandVision acquisition), around 900 M€/yr pre-tax, kept in the model's GAAP base (never stripped out, unlike management's 'adjusted' measure) - explains most of the structural gap between the model's GAAP EPS and the market consensus, which is generally followed on an adjusted/non-GAAP basis.

Myopia management (+25% in H1 26, +22% in 2025) and AI glasses (units sold up roughly x1,7 in 2025, US/international ramp-up under way) remain the two structural drivers of organic growth, with a contribution that gradually normalises (broader base), bringing group growth back down towards a high end of the 'mid-single-digit' range pace over the medium term.

High net debt (13,4 Md€ at end-June 2026, ND/EBITDA ~2,0x) on the back of bolt-on acquisitions (Optegra, Top Charoen, Signifeye, Faro...) and of buybacks tied to employee plans; annual free cash flow (~2,8 Md€ in 2025) funds these uses without further material re-leveraging - the model assumes a gradual decline in net debt towards ~8,8 Md€ by 2030.

The share count rises modestly each year through the scrip dividend option (the share of shareholders electing the scrip varying widely from one year to the next, from 9% to 70% depending on the year) and employee share ownership plans, partly offset by the buybacks dedicated to compensation plans - the model assumes a net drift of around +0,6-0,8%/yr.

The new long-term horizon communicated in February 2026 (succeeding the 2022 CMD target, exceeded on revenue as early as 2025 but not on margin) guides to 'solid growth' in revenue and to adjusted operating margin progression 'broadly in line' with that of revenue, at constant FX, with no precise quantification - it serves as a directional guardrail rather than a calibrated target for the model's 2026-2030 trajectory.

hypothese.text:
== THESIS SUMMARY ==
Vertically integrated world leader in optics-eyewear (Essilor lenses, Luxottica frames/retail, GrandVision) with a widening med-tech/AI frontier: Meta smart glasses (Ray-Ban, Oakley, Display), myopia management (Stellest), hearing (Nuance Audio) and ophthalmic clinics. The thesis combines a defensive prescription core, pricing power through vertical integration, and free optionality on the wearables wave - Q2 26 kept H2 guidance qualitative (solid organic at constant FX, gross margin up) against demanding comps.

== THESIS READ ==
- The wearables leg is becoming material: Meta partnership deepening across product generations. Watch: any first quantified disclosure of smart-glasses revenue - it would force a re-segmentation of the model.
- Core organic holds mid-single-digit with margin drift toward the ~19-20% ambition of the 2022 plan. Watch: H2 organic vs the demanding comp base.
- Share count creeps UP (~+4M/yr, employee/partner plans) - a quiet dilution the model carries explicitly. Watch: any buyback offset.

== SPECIAL FACTORS ==
Semi-annual P&L cadence (T1/T3 are revenue-only) - quarterlyEPS is semester-structured. Base keeps ~900M/yr PPA amortization (definitional wedge vs adjusted consensus, documented in the scorecard). Bridge caveat flagged: projected finNet is a fitted block bundling leases and growing minority/other drag - it rises while net debt falls because the flat 68.5% conversion embeds that drag; to decompose with full statements. priorEPS null (young fiche).

== PARAMETERS & WATCH-LIST ==
2026: revenue 29.9bn, EBIT 4.26bn (14.2%), net 2,918M / EPS 6.24; 2027-2030: ~6.5%/yr revenue, EBIT margin to 15.4%, deleveraging 12.5 -> 8.8bn. ETR 26%, minorities -80M. Watch: finNet decomposition; Stellest/Nuance ramp; Meta partnership economics.

== CATALYSTS ==
Q3 revenue (Oct); Meta Display sell-through; FY26 results (Feb 2027); med-tech regulatory milestones.
